name: CyBe R (Robot)
summary: Entry-level stationary 3D concrete printer: an ABB industrial robot arm on a floor-fixed frame that prints concrete elements in a ring around itself, for precast production, prototyping and research.

germany.statusNote: EU maker (Netherlands) sells directly through its sales team and contact form, with a published 'price from' figure ex works; no German distributor found. CyBe says it distributes worldwide and the printers are modular for transport. The 'from €49,000' price is marked 'only while supply lasts'.

priceEur.note: 'Price from €49,000*' with '*Price ex works, based on standard dimensions, only while supply lasts!'; tax basis not stated. The FAQ on the same page gives older figures: 'CyBe R (Robot) €150,000 Ex Works, CyBe RC (Robot Crawler) €195,000 Ex Works, and CyBe G (Gantry) €285,000 Ex Works'.

sellers.name: CyBe Construction B.V.
sellers.note: Oss, Netherlands; the contact form has the option 'I want to buy a printer'. Price is ex works, standard dimensions; transport and import taxes are paid by the buyer.

specs.label: Print range (standard)
specs.conditions: donut-shaped area around the printer; the page lists it as length × width × height but gives two figures

specs.label: Print speed
specs.quote: At 500 millimeters per second, CyBe printers have the fastest print speed in the market.

specs.label: Robot
specs.value: ABB robot arm on a floor-fixed metal frame
specs.quote: The ABB robotic arm is attached on a metal frame which is secured to the floor.

specs.label: Training included
specs.conditions: CyBe supplies hardware, software, materials, service and designs
specs.quote: CyBe supplies the full package: hardware, software, materials, service, designs, and 10-day training at any location.

specs.label: Operating crew
specs.conditions: one at the control unit, one at the mortar mixer (stated for CyBe printers in general)
specs.quote: The printer is operated by just two persons

notes: Stationary: the arm stands on a frame bolted to the floor; it does not move between prints.
Needs a mortar mixing and pumping unit; CyBe sells its own CyBe Mortar.
Meant for off-site, facility-based printing (precast, prototypes, research).

images.alt: CyBe R stationary 3D concrete printer with its robot arm on a fixed frame

evidence.task: Printed five concrete city benches for Dura Vermeer for the city of Haarlem, off-site in CyBe's facility (35 minutes per bench)
evidence.note: Shown as the application spotlight on the CyBe R page; the text says the benches were printed off-site, and a caption adds that the in-situ bench print 'was possible with CyBe R'.
